summary: Adds a helper to extract the browser family from a request's User-Agent header. Naive parsing with no null handling and incorrect assumptions about the format.

expected_findings.description: Missing None check. request.user_agent can be None or have a None string attribute when the header is missing. Accessing .string on None raises AttributeError, and .split on None raises AttributeError. Should handle missing UA explicitly and return a sentinel like 'unknown'.

Incorrect parsing assumption. Most real User-Agent strings start with 'Mozilla/5.0' regardless of browser — Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge all do. This function will return 'mozilla' for nearly every modern browser, making it useless for its stated purpose. Use werkzeug's user_agent parser or a library like ua-parser.
Parameter 'request' has no type annotation. Other functions in this module type-annotate. Should be 'Request' or similar.

should_not_flag: Lowercasing the result — that's fine, even sensible for case-insensitive comparison.
The function being a thin wrapper — appropriate scope for a helper.
Lack of tests — fair to mention but not blocking on a 4-line helper.
notes_for_arbiter: Both F1 and F2 are real and findable on careful read. F2 is the more interesting one because the code 'works' (doesn't crash) but produces wrong output. A reviewer who only catches F1 (the crash) and misses F2 (the wrongness) has caught the obvious half. Classic Devon: enthusiastic, has the right shape but didn't read the actual format of real UA strings.
